Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer Added text based ATC clauses JUSTIFICATION FOR PAINTING OF SECURITY EQUIPMENT The existing security equipment installed at the premises, comprising Portable Guard Cabins – Qty. 04, Bul let Proof Morchas – Qty. 12, Iron Barricades – Qty. 10 and Spike Barriers – Qty. 04, is exposed to outdoor e nvironmental conditions such as rain, moisture, dust, sunlight and atmospheric humidity. Continuous expo sure to these conditions can result in deterioration of the existing paint coating, corrosion/rusting of metal surfaces, and gradual weakening of the equipment. Painting of the above security equipment is therefore necessary to: 1. Prevent rust and corrosion: Proper surface preparation and application of suitable anti-corrosive primer and protective paint will provide a barrier against moisture and atmospheric exposure. 2. Increase service life: A durable protective coating will reduce deterioration of metal components and hel p extend the useful service life of the equipment. 3. Improve durability: Repainting will protect exposed metal surfaces from weathering, abrasion and routin e operational use. 4. Maintain structural condition: Early treatment of rusted and deteriorated areas will help prevent further corrosion and associated damage. 5. Improve visibility and identification: Properly painted barricades, spike barriers and other security equip ment will remain clearly visible and identifiable, particularly during night and adverse weather conditions. 6. Maintain appearance and upkeep: Uniform painting will improve the overall appearance and demonstrat e proper maintenance of security installations. 7. Reduce future maintenance expenditure: Preventive anti-corrosion treatment can minimize the need for frequent repairs, replacement of corroded components and premature renewal of equipment. Accordingly, painting and protective coating of the security equipment is considered necessary as a preve ntive maintenance measure for long-term durability, rust protection, safety and proper upkeep. DETAILS OF SECURITY EQUIPMENT Sr. No.| Description of Equipment| Quantity 1| Portable Guard Cabin 04 Nos. (Colour - Smoke Grey) 2| Bullet Proof Morcha 12 Nos. (Colour - Smoke Grey) 3| Iron Barricade 10 Nos. (Royal Blue) 4| Spike Barrier 04 Nos. (Red, Yellow, Black) 5| Electric Siren 01 Nos. (Colour - Smoke Grey) SCOPE OF WORK The work shall generally include the following activities: 1. Inspection and Surface Preparation - Inspect all equipment and identify areas affected by rust, peeling paint, corrosion, dirt, grease or damage d coating. - Remove loose, flaking and defective paint by suitable mechanical means such as wire brushing, scraping, sanding or other approved methods.

- Remove rust and corrosion from affected metal surfaces to obtain a sound and clean surface. - Clean the surfaces thoroughly to remove dust, grease, oil, moisture and other contaminants before painti ng. - Any minor surface defects requiring treatment shall be attended to before application of the coating syst em. 2. Anti-Corrosive Primer - Apply one suitable coat of approved anti-corrosive metal primer over the prepared metal surfaces. - Particular attention shall be given to joints, edges, corners, welds, exposed metal portions and areas prev iously affected by rust. - Primer shall be applied uniformly and allowed to dry properly in accordance with the manufacturer's reco mmendations. 3. Protective Finish Coating - Apply two coats of approved exterior-grade/enamel or equivalent protective metal paint suitable for outd oor exposure. - The selected paint shall provide good adhesion, weather resistance and protection against moisture and corrosion. - Each coat shall be allowed adequate drying/curing time before application of the subsequent coat. - Final colour shall be as approved by the Engineer/Competent Authority and, where applicable, shall confo rm to the existing security/identification colour scheme. 4. Treatment of Rusted/Damaged Areas - Heavily rusted areas shall receive additional surface preparation and treatment as required. - Severely deteriorated portions, if any, shall be brought to the notice of the Engineer/Competent Authority before undertaking repairs or replacement. - Painting shall not be carried out over loose rust, loose paint or contaminated surfaces. 5. Workmanship and Protection - Painting shall be carried out with proper workmanship to achieve a smooth, uniform and continuous finis h without runs, sagging, peeling, missed portions or excessive brush marks. - Adjacent surfaces, equipment and flooring shall be adequately protected against paint splashes and dam age. - The security equipment shall remain functional after completion of painting; moving/operating parts shall not be jammed or obstructed by paint. - Barricades and spike barriers shall be painted in a manner that does not interfere with their intended sec urity function. 6. Final Inspection and Cleaning - On completion, all painted surfaces shall be inspected for uniformity, coverage, adhesion and visible defe cts. - Any defective, missed or damaged portion shall be rectified by the contractor at no additional cost where attributable to workmanship. - The work area shall be cleaned and all debris, loose paint material, masking material and waste generate d during the work shall be removed. - The completed equipment shall be handed over in a clean, properly painted and serviceable condition. EXPECTED OUTCOME Upon completion, all 04 Portable Guard Cabins, 12 Bullet Proof Morchas, 10 Iron Barricades and 04 Spike B arriers shall have a properly prepared and protective paint system providing improved resistance against r ust, corrosion, moisture, weathering and general environmental exposure. The work will help preserve the equipment, enhance its service life, maintain visibility and appearance, and ensure proper preventive mai ntenance of the security installations. The oil paint used shall be of a reputed brand and approved quality. - All tools, equipment, accessories, and consumable materials required for painting the security equipment shall be arranged and brought by the service provider/vendor. - Before commencing the painting work, the paint brand, quality, and shade shall be verified and approved by the buyer’s authorized representative. - The service provider shall ensure that all necessary materials and accessories are available at the site be fore starting the work. - No additional charges shall be payable by the buyer for any materials, tools, accessories, transportation, or other requirements necessary to complete the painting work. .
